name: Puttalam–Chilaw
locator: West coast panel, Puttalam to Chilaw via Mundel
note: Trace follows the inland stroke beside Mundel Lake and the printed road past Battul Oya. A short join crosses the horizontal sheet fold.

name: Chilaw–Negombo
locator: West coast panel, Chilaw to Negombo via Madampe and Marawila
note: The line crosses the printed river at Chilaw and runs inland of the coast and lagoon. The continuation to Colombo requires separate tracing.

name: Kankesanturai–Point Pedro
locator: Jaffna peninsula panels, north coast past Maviddapuram and Vallai
note: Short join across the vertical sheet fold. The coastal stroke is distinct from the inland Jaffna road network.

name: Anuradhapura–Trincomalee
locator: North-Central and Eastern panels, via Mihintale and Horowupotana
note: Follows the double road line through the printed rest houses and joins matching ends across the sheet folds. The urban approach is generalized.

name: Mihintale junction–Medawachchiya
locator: North-Central panel, junction near Mihintale to Medawachchiya R.H.
note: Starts at the junction east of Anuradhapura. The trace follows the paired road strokes east of the separately printed proposed railway.

name: Dambulla–Matale
locator: Central panel, Dambulla R.H. to Matale via Nalanda
note: The road runs on the west side of the vertical sheet fold. Its meeting with the Matale railway is generalized in the town symbol.

name: Matara–Tangalla
locator: Southern coastal panels, Matara to Tangalla R.H.
note: The road leaves the Matara town area and continues along the coast. Short joins at the town and sheet fold are generalized.

name: Tangalla–Ambalantota
locator: Southern coastal panel, Tangalla through Ranna to Ambalantota R.H.
note: Trace ends at the printed Ambalantota junction. The road to Hambantota is visible farther east and awaits a separate trace.

name: Anuradhapura–Dambulla
locator: North-Central panel, Anuradhapura to Dambulla via the Kekirawa area
note: The southeastern road leaves the Trincomalee road near Anuradhapura. In the southern half of this trace the double road stroke and the dashed proposed railway run close to each other.
